The '''1977–78 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|75th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|46th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The club did not compete in UEFA competitions for the first time since the [[1954–55 Real Madrid CF season|1954–55]] season. During the summer, the team was reinforced with the arrivals of: Argentine defender [[Enrique Wolff]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1979/07/05/deportes/299973602_850215.html|title=I leave Real Madrid because some Rules...|work=El País|date=4 July 1979|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> and high-expected Forward [[Juanito (footballer, born 1954)|Juanito]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1977/08/30/deportes/241740022_850215.html|title=Juanito, The New Great White Hope|language=Spanish|work=El País|date=29 August 1977|access-date=2 July 2020|author=Alfredo Relaño}}</ref> from [[Burgos CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1976/11/21/deportes/217378801_850215.html|date=20 November 1976|access-date=2 July 2020|work=El País|title=Juanito Will Play the Next Season at Bernabeu Stadium.|language=Spanish}}</ref> Bernabeu traveled to West Germany seeking to replace [[Paul Breitner]] by signing [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]]'s star [[Herbert Wimmer]], but once he saw midfielder [[Uli Stielike]] play, he changed his mind and transferred the latter into the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1977/04/30/deportes/231199212_850215.html|title=Stielike, new Real Madrid football player|work=El País|date=29 April 1977|access-date=2 July 2020|author=Juan José Paradinas}}</ref> 

President Santiago Bernabéu suffered a [[bowel obstruction]] on 29 August 1977 and was transferred to a hospital for emergency treatment being diagnosed with cancer days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.lavanguardia.es/preview/1978/06/03/pagina-49/33736408/pdf.html?search=Santiago%20Bernab%C3%A9u|title=Yesterday, Don Santiago Bernabéu Passed Away|work=La Vanguardia|date=3 June 1978|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> After three seasons, [[Miljan Miljanić]] left the club on 8 September 1977 signing an agreement with [[Santiago Bernabéu (footballer)|Santiago Bernabéu]] at the hospital in a bizarre event.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1977/09/09/deportes/242604002_850215.html|work=El País|title=Miljanic did not lose the smile on his Departure|language=Spanish|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> Then, [[Luis Molowny]] was appointed by Raimundo Saporta as the new head coach. Also, Saporta was appointed as Acting President on 3 September 1977 due to Bernabeu health issues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1977/09/09/deportes/242604005_850215.html |title=Saporta, a True Solution|work=El País|date=8 September 1977|access-date=2 July 2020|language=Spanish|author=Julian Garcia Candu}}</ref>

In spite of the turmoil, the club clinched its 18th League title ever closing the season on 7 May 1978 six points above runners-up [[FC Barcelona]]. Chairman Santiago Bernabéu died on 2 June 1978 ending Real Madrid's most successful era, with the club clinching 6 European Cups and 16 League titles under his presidency.
